02 — Research Focus

Four disciplines, one operating problem

My work sits at the intersection of power engineering and machine intelligence: keeping renewable-heavy grids secure, stable, and low-cost while an adversary — or the weather — actively works against them.

Power Systems

AC/DC optimal power flow, unit commitment, and stochastic scheduling of wind-integrated networks on IEEE benchmark systems.

Cyber-Security

Moving Target Defense against false-data-injection attacks, learned defense policies, and cost-aware cyber-physical resilience.

Optimization

Multi-objective, risk-aware formulations — augmented ε-constraint, CVaR, bi-level and metaheuristic solvers for large-scale problems.

Artificial Intelligence

Deep RL (PPO, DQN), generative models (GAN, CGAN) and Bi-LSTM forecasting embedded directly into grid decision-making.

03 — Proposed PhD Direction

Proposed PhD research — multi-agent RL for the smart grid

A cooperative multi-agent PPO framework under centralized-training / decentralized-execution, paired with a conditional GAN for uncertainty — targeting wind-curtailment, operating cost, and network loss on the IEEE 118-bus system.

Three coordinated agent types — wind-curtailment, EV-fleet, and storage / substation — learn jointly while a conditional GAN synthesizes optimistic, realistic, and pessimistic scenarios offline and adapts online under distributional drift.

STAGE 01

Generative uncertainty

A conditional GAN pretrained offline to synthesize realistic wind & EV scenarios, fine-tuned online when drift is detected.

STAGE 02

Cooperative MARL

PPO agents trained centrally, executed locally — coordinating curtailment, charging, and storage in real time.

STAGE 03

Tri-objective control

Curtailment mitigation, cost minimization, and active-loss reduction resolved on the IEEE 118-bus network.

IEEE Trans. Industrial Informatics Published · 2026

A PPO-GAN-Enabled Moving Target Defense for Cyber-Resilient and Cost-Aware Power System Scheduling

+
Abstract

Rising renewable penetration and increasingly sophisticated false-data-injection attacks impose severe security and operating pressures on modern grids. This work develops a reinforcement-learning Moving Target Defense whose core is a Proximal Policy Optimization agent that learns an adaptive perturbation policy — jointly choosing reactance magnitudes and line locations to maximize attack-detection rate while capping the cost increment. A GAN acts as an adversary synthesizing stealthy attack vectors, forcing the defender to adapt under uncertainty, while battery energy storage offsets the economic burden of defensive actions.

Objectives
  • Learn an adaptive line-reactance perturbation policy with PPO under strict cost limits.
  • Model a GAN adversary that generates stealthy attacks to stress-test the defense.
  • Use battery storage as a flexibility resource enabling stronger yet cost-feasible perturbations.
  • Validate on IEEE 118-bus: BES lifts detection ≈125% at <0.02% cost; robust to 17% stealth attacks.

Reliability Eng. & System Safety IF ≈ 11.0 Published · 2026

Enhancing Power Grid Cybersecurity Against FDI Attacks via Deep Q-Network-Based Moving Target Defense

+
Abstract

False-data-injection attacks threaten both the stability and the economics of modern power systems. This paper proposes an Intelligent Moving Target Defense that dynamically modifies the reactances of selected transmission lines using a Deep Q-Network, obscuring system parameters from attackers with minimal disruption to power flow and cost. Unlike Pareto-based MO-MTD or smallest-principal-angle methods, the learned policy perturbs the most influential lines to maximize detectability under a cost-aware reward.

Objectives
  • Design a DQN agent that selects high-impact lines for reactance perturbation.
  • Balance security and efficiency through a cost-aware reward structure.
  • Test against stealthy, topology-aware, economic, sparse, adaptive & coordinated attacks.
  • Achieve 91.3% detection at <0.0003% OPF cost on IEEE 118-bus — up to 99% cost reduction vs. benchmarks.

Journal of Cleaner Production IF ≈ 9.7 Published · 2023

Wind Curtailment Mitigation in Presence of Battery Energy Storage and Electric Vehicle: A Comprehensive Multi-Objective Decision-Support Framework

+
Abstract

Fluctuating wind power and plug-in hybrid electric vehicles inject substantial uncertainty into system scheduling. This work introduces a two-stage, scenario-based decision-support framework: the first stage solves unit commitment to minimize operating cost and re-optimizes dispatchable wind; the second sizes battery storage while intelligent parking lots issue price signals guiding EV participation in economic dispatch. An augmented ε-constraint method captures the Pareto set, from which an operator-preference decision method selects the final solution.

Objectives
  • Mitigate wind curtailment under high renewable penetration and EV uncertainty.
  • Co-optimize thermal unit commitment, storage sizing, and EV dispatch.
  • Apply augmented ε-constraint with correlated stochastic scenarios for robustness.
  • Cut total operating cost by 68% and battery sizing by 6.1% on the IEEE 30-bus system.

Renewable Energy IF ≈ 9.0 Published · 2024

Accelerating Optimal Scheduling Prediction in Power Systems: A Multi-Faceted GAN-Assisted Prediction Framework

+
Abstract

This study enhances scheduling optimality through a two-stage optimization coupled with a deep model for Optimal Scheduling Prediction. A Bidirectional LSTM first forecasts wind power; a convolutional GAN then synthesizes scenarios from the preceding ten days of predictions, feeding the downstream optimization. Outputs train a deep predictor that reproduces optimal dispatch almost instantly — combining forecasting, generation, and learned optimization surrogates in one pipeline.

Objectives
  • Forecast wind power accurately with a Bi-LSTM front end.
  • Generate realistic scenarios via a convolutional GAN for robust scheduling.
  • Train a deep surrogate that predicts optimal dispatch in real time.
  • Reach 10-day-ahead dispatch in 0.38 s, error <0.001, 92% correlation; OPTUNA tuning +24%.

IET Renewable Power Generation Published · 2024

Intelligent Parking Lot Power Management: Augmented Epsilon-Constraint Concept with Correlation Analysis

+
Abstract

This paper tackles decision-making in energy-resource management through a tri-objective optimization that drives operating cost, emissions, and load-shedding toward their ideal points while maximizing responsive-demand participation. Photovoltaic and wind outputs are treated as scenario-based stochastic variables, and plug-in electric vehicles are organized as intelligent parking lots to raise network flexibility. Each scenario's multi-objective problem is solved by an augmented ε-constraint method enriched with correlation-coefficient analysis.

Objectives
  • Formulate a tri-objective model balancing cost, emissions, and load-shedding.
  • Integrate PHEV intelligent parking lots to boost flexibility under RES uncertainty.
  • Solve per-scenario Pareto fronts with augmented ε-constraint + correlation analysis.
  • Validate accuracy on a modified IEEE 83-bus test system.

IEEE Conference AI · Optimization

Comparative Analysis of Metaheuristic Approaches for Optimal Routing of Electric Vehicles with Simultaneous Pickup and Delivery

+
Abstract

This paper compares metaheuristic solvers for the Electric Vehicle Routing Problem with Simultaneous Pickup and Delivery. A mathematical model incorporating vehicle-capacity and battery-energy limits is formulated, and Genetic Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, and Bat Algorithm are implemented with priority-based encoding and a route-splitting repair mechanism. Across randomly generated instances, all three yield high-quality solutions; PSO offers the best quality-efficiency balance.

Objectives
  • Model EV routing with simultaneous pickup/delivery under capacity and battery limits.
  • Compare GA, PSO, and Bat Algorithm on solution quality and runtime.
  • Handle infeasible routes with a battery-aware route-splitting repair.
  • Identify PSO as best-balanced — optimal in 4 of 6 cases and lowest cost at larger scale.
